How do I build my own optical probe like the MY015-D?

Fig 2 · Build your own

    Break it

    Parts list, with the values the model picked

    3D-printed cup and capPLA, Ø34 mm, 12 cm³ of plastic
    Infrared LEDVishay TSAL4400, 940 nm, 3 mm
    Phototransistorams OSRAM SFH 309 FA-4 (daylight filter)
    LED resistor680 Ω for 5.2 mA
    Pull-up resistor39 kΩ
    Round boardØ14 mm
    Ring magnet27 × 16 × 5 mm, N42
    Cable4 cores: 5V red, GND black, TX white, RX green
    USB-serial boardFTDI FT232RL with USB-C (a CH340 board works too)
    Heat-shrinkØ6 → Ø3 mm sleeve
    Test standM10 fender washer on a 12.5 mm printed riser, Ø20 mm mirror 12 mm below the face

    The big idea: two parts make the probe, one LED to talk and one light sensor to listen; everything else holds them in the right place.

    Where the numbers come from
    • LED: Vishay TSAL4400 datasheet: 940 nm, ±25°, 100 mA maximum, VF 1.35 V at 100 mA and 2.6 V at 1 A, 36 mW/sr at 100 mA. The forward voltage at 5 mA (≈1.08 V) is fitted between those two points with a diode curve (n ≈ 2 assumed), and light is taken as proportional to current: both are estimates.
    • Sensor: ams OSRAM SFH 309 FA datasheet (values read from v1.3, 2018): 730–1120 nm (the plain SFH 309: 380–1150 nm), ±12°, group -4 gives 1.0–2.0 mA at 0.5 mW/cm², 50 nA dark current at most, 0.2 V saturated, chip 2.4–2.8 mm behind the tip. The model uses the middle of group -4.
    • Serial chip: FTDI FT232R datasheet (FT_000053), VCCIO = 5 V: inputs switch between 1.0 and 1.5 V and have a 200 kΩ pull-up inside; outputs sink 2 mA (standard drive) or 6 mA (high drive, set in its EEPROM with FT_Prog) at 0.4 V, 24 mA absolute maximum. So 5.2 mA needs the high-drive setting; at standard drive, add a transistor.
    • Spacing 6.5 mm between LED and sensor: the footprints of twam's open IEC 62056-21 probe PCB (SFH 487-2 at x = −146.75, SFH 309 FA-4 at x = −153.25). Ring magnet 27 × 16 × 5 mm N42: the parts list of the volkszaehler.org TTL read head (twam uses 26.75 × 16 × 5). I could not read the standard's own drawing (IEC 62056-21 is paywalled), so treat both as copied from working designs, not from the standard.
    • Mirror gap 12 mm: the model's best echo for 6.5 mm spacing and the sensor's ±12°. Pull-up 39 kΩ: the smallest E12 value that pulls RX below 1.0 V with 1.5× margin on that echo.
    • Guesses, not measured: daylight reaching the sensor chip on the stand (1 part in 1000), the share of sunlight the sensor answers to (¼ with the filter, ½ without), 100 lm per watt for sunlight, 0.9 for the mirror, 3 mm³/s for the printer (so the print takes about 65 min).
    • The meter's reply /WPA5WM-ULTRA-15 at 300 baud, 7E1, is the invented meter from figure 1; the noise you see at other speeds is what a UART sampling at the wrong speed really reads (simulated).
    • Phone front cameras often lack the infrared-cut filter that rear cameras have, which is why the LED shows purple on the selfie camera: a common hobby tip, not true of every phone.
